audits.title: 133 A Quality Improvement Project to Improve the Appropriateness of Acute Clinic Referrals to a Local ENT Department Using an Electronic Booking System
audits.standard: Locally created referral guideline based on protocols from major UK trusts
audits.setting: Local ENT department acute clinic (Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Luton)

cycle1.result: 29% of referrals inappropriate (50% too complex, 45% not acute, 5% double-bookings); nasal fracture reviews within 10 days one third of the time; 37% no contact number; 13.8% incorrect or unclear clinical information.

audits.other_findings: An electronic referral system and guideline dissemination were introduced ahead of a planned re-audit in September 2021.
audits.citation: Parmar V, Maity A, Singh P. 133 A Quality Improvement Project to Improve the Appropriateness of Acute Clinic Referrals to a Local ENT Department Using an Electronic Booking System. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac039.076.

audits.title: 1508 Acute ENT Clinic Audit
audits.standard: ENT UK guidance: SHO-led acute clinic maximum 6 patients; local standard that children are seen first
audits.setting: SHO-led acute ENT clinic, East & North Hertfordshire NHS Trust, Stevenage

cycle1.result: Only 8 clinics had maximum 6 patients; 27 clinics (77.2%) had more than 7 booked; children seen first in 8 clinics (22.9%).

audits.other_findings: 69.8% of patients had unsuitable referrals per guideline; stricter referral system proposed.
audits.citation: Bondje S, Tanna R, Stephens J. 1508 Acute ENT Clinic Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.168.

audits.title: Rapid access rather than open access leads to improved effectiveness of an ENT emergency clinic.
audits.standard: National guidelines on safe clinic numbers

cycle1.result: 45% attended without primary care assessment; mean wait 75 minutes; clinic numbers above safe levels; 60% of attendances inappropriate.

audits.intervention: Open access clinic changed to appointment-based Rapid Access Clinic with trained triage nurse, improved record keeping and formal post-consultation communication.

cycle2.result: 43% fewer patients; clinic numbers at safe levels; mean waiting time fell 70% to 22 minutes; inappropriate referrals halved.

audits.citation: Smyth C, Moran M, Diver C, Hampton S. Rapid access rather than open access leads to improved effectiveness of an ENT emergency clinic. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2013;2(1):u200524.w996. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u200524.w996. PMID: 26734173.

audits.title: Senior triaging of ENT emergency clinic referrals alleviates pressures on the outpatient department.
audits.setting: ENT emergency clinic, Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Clinic session overbookings 85%; inappropriate referral appointments 22%

audits.intervention: GP telephone referrals directed to the on-call ENT registrar 8am-1pm Monday to Friday for senior triage
audits.citation: Mughal Z, Seigel J, Basu S. Senior triaging of ENT emergency clinic referrals alleviates pressures on the outpatient department. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2022;104(2):117-120. doi:10.1308/rcsann.2021.0068. PMID: 34813383.

audits.title: Sustained Improvement in Paediatric ENT Emergency Referral Accuracy Through a Multimodal Educational Strategy: A Longitudinal Study.
audits.standard: Local Trust paediatric ENT emergency clinic referral guidelines (100% adherence)
audits.setting: SHO-led paediatric ENT emergency clinic, Queen's Medical Centre, Nottingham (tertiary centre)
audits.intervention: Targeted junior doctor teaching, dissemination of referral criteria via online platforms and a poster campaign.

cycle2.result: Guideline-compliant referrals increased to 74.0%, sustained across subsequent cycles.

audits.other_findings: Six cycles in total; common inappropriate referrals were cerumen impaction and discharging ear.
audits.citation: Simon R, Daniel M. Sustained Improvement in Paediatric ENT Emergency Referral Accuracy Through a Multimodal Educational Strategy: A Longitudinal Study. Cureus. 2025;17(12):e100306. doi:10.7759/cureus.100306. PMID: 41473923.
